# Packages published in the self-hosted opkg repo but NOT installed in the
# image, so users can `opkg install` them on demand.
#
# Why they are not in the image:
#   - size. OpenClash alone pulls ruby, haproxy and dnsmasq-full; the sysupgrade
#     image is ~35 MB and these would roughly double it.
#   - TTL. OpenClash installs its own redirect rules that can bypass the
#     nftables chain luci-app-qmodem-ttlfw4 owns, and a correct TTL on the
#     wire is the point of this firmware. Installing it is a user choice.
#
# Dependencies are listed explicitly because the repo is filtered against the
# image manifest: these packages are absent from it, so opkg would not pull
# their dependencies in automatically. The list is the transitive closure of
# every root below, derived from the built .ipk control files - not a guess.
#
# One package name per line. Blank lines and # ignored.

# --- AdGuard Home ---
adguardhome
luci-app-adguardhome

# --- banIP ---
banip
luci-app-banip

# --- SmartDNS ---
smartdns
luci-app-smartdns

# --- iptables-nft shim -----------------------------------------------------
# mwan3, sqm-scripts, nikki and OpenClash all shell out to iptables at
# runtime (mwan3 49 references, OpenClash 362, nikki 16), so they cannot work
# without it. We ship the nft-backed shim, NOT legacy iptables:
#
#   iptables-nft  PROVIDES=iptables, DEFAULT_VARIANT=1, and every binary it
#                 installs is *-nft (iptables-nft, iptables-nft-restore, ...)
#   xtables-nft   DEPENDS=kmod-nft-compat + libnftnl - it writes nft rules
#
# So this is nftables under an iptables-compatible name, which keeps
# firewall4 and the TTL chain intact. xtables-legacy is never pulled in.
iptables-nft
ip6tables-nft
iptables-mod-conntrack-extra
iptables-mod-ipopt
# These come out of the kernel build (they are already produced for the target
# feed) and are listed here so the repo publishes them; there is no package
# directory of their own, so the build step skips them and that is correct.
kmod-ipt-core
kmod-ipt-ipset
kmod-ifb
kmod-nft-compat
kmod-sched-cake
kmod-sched-core
# tc is a virtual name: tc-tiny / tc-full / tc-bpf all PROVIDES:=tc. The real
# package is tc-tiny, so name that or opkg reports "tc" as unavailable.
tc-tiny
ipset

# --- SQM (traffic shaping) ---
# The cake/hybrid qdiscs are pure tc and contain zero iptables calls; only
# simple.qos uses iptables, for ingress policing. The iptables-nft shim above
# covers that too, so every SQM mode works.
luci-app-sqm
sqm-scripts

# --- mwan3 (multi-WAN failover) ---
mwan3
luci-app-mwan3

# --- Nikki (mihomo) ---
# nikki depends on "mihomo"; the feed's mihomo-meta package provides it.
luci-app-nikki
mihomo-meta
nikki
yq

# --- HomeProxy (sing-box) ---
luci-app-homeproxy
sing-box
firewall4
ucode-mod-digest

# --- passwall2 geo add-ons ----------------------------------------------
# Stripped from the image because the node is VLESS over plain ws: no
# geoip:/geosite: routing rule matches, xray loads the .dat files lazily, and
# passwall2 disables geoview cleanly when the binary is missing. Install these
# if you add geo-based routing rules in passwall2.
geoview
v2ray-geoip
v2ray-geosite
chinadns-ng
# --- PassWall v1 (Lua, fw4 capable) - IN THE IMAGE since 1.2.39 -----------
# Vendored at packages/luci-app-passwall (4.66-8) and shipped disabled. It was
# listed here until 1.2.38, which never worked: this repo is filtered against
# the image manifest, so its three hard deps (dns2socks, dns2tcp, microsocks)
# were not published, opkg could not resolve them, and the install failed -
# the "4.66-8 is inaccessible" symptom. All four are in the image now, so they
# are deliberately absent from this list; ci_check_packages rejects any of
# them reappearing here.
# --- OpenClash (clash) ---
luci-app-openclash
haproxy
ruby
ruby-yaml
libncursesw6
dnsmasq-full
bash
curl
ca-bundle
ip
ip-full
kmod-dummy
kmod-inet-diag
kmod-netlink-diag
kmod-nft-tproxy
kmod-tun
unzip
coreutils-nohup
ucode
# --- Tailscale ---
# Out of the image: the daemon idles at ~13 MB RSS for a feature most units
# never configure, and the binary is ~10 MB. /etc/init.d/byte-tailscale-gate
# ships regardless, so an on-demand install still starts tailscaled only once
# credentials exist.
tailscale
luci-app-tailscale-community
